in_scope: Static inspection of milp.py source code
Mathematical analysis of constraint and objective structure

key_findings.F1: The MILP optimization problem (360 variables, 12 constraint types, all bounds) is fully mathematically transferable to both Option A and Option B without modification.
key_findings.F2: scipy.optimize.milp exposes ONLY a single-objective interface to HiGHS. Multi-objective HiGHS capabilities (if they exist) are NOT accessible via the scipy wrapper.
key_findings.F3: Stage 1 (p_unmet), Stage 3 (p_diesel, u_diesel, v_start), and Stage 4 (p_curt_sol, p_curt_wind) objective terms exist in the current code and require only decomposition (not formulation) for transfer.
key_findings.F4: Stage 2 (terminal battery reserve) has NO current objective coefficient. This is a NEW formulation requirement for both options. It is NOT a transfer item — it is new engineering work.
key_findings.F5: Battery degradation penalties (p_chg, p_dis) exist in the current objective but have no explicit assignment in the governed 4-stage hierarchy. This requires a governance decision.
key_findings.F6: highspy is not installed in the current POLARIS environment. Option B requires highspy installation as a prerequisite.
key_findings.F7: HiGHS stable MILP multi-objective (as opposed to LP multi-objective) is not confirmed as a production feature in HiGHS 1.x stable releases. This is an open dependency for Option B.
key_findings.F8: Option A and Option B are analytically equivalent under: same objective order, zero epsilon tolerance, same feasibility region, same HiGHS underlying solver. This equivalence is analytical — not empirically verified (empirical verification requires execution, which is outside this audit scope).
